nodes.name: `lower_trait_object_ty` lowers bare trait types in method signatures and triggers object-safety checks during HIR type lowering, directly exposing the recursive `A`/`B` signature cycle
`replace_dummy_self_with_error` is part of trait-object/self-type repair during lowering, but is only indirectly related to this cycle and less likely to be the primary trigger

`prohibit_or_lint_bare_trait_object_ty` handles bare-trait-object diagnostics in HIR type lowering and can defer/report missing-`dyn` problems after object-safety/signature queries have already been entered, contributing to delayed ICE surfacing

`maybe_suggest_impl_trait` is part of the missing-`dyn` diagnostic/suggestion path and consults surrounding function-signature context, reinforcing that error handling occurs in a delayed lint/suggestion flow rather than preventing the recursive query early

`object_safety_violations_for_trait` inspects each trait's associated items and object-safety constraints, which can force method-signature analysis for mutually recursive trait-typed methods and thus close the query cycle

`object_safety_violations_for_assoc_item` evaluates per-method object-safety of trait items; for methods using other traits as parameter/return types, this can recursively demand signature/object-safety computation of the counterpart trait
`virtual_call_violations_for_method` checks method dispatchability/object-safety properties and is a likely point where method signature details are queried during object-safety determination
`contains_illegal_self_type_reference` / `IllegalSelfTypeVisitor` are mostly about illegal `Self` references rather than mutual trait-type recursion, so they are only weakly related to this ICE path
`is_vtable_safe_method` contributes to per-method object-safety evaluation, but is less directly evidenced than the core violation collectors as the cycle origin
